title: Settlement Agreements Consumer Terms: Default of an Accepted Settlement and Release of the Remainder
content:
# Settlement Agreements — Default and Release of the Remainder

**Clause 1 — When a settlement defaults.** An accepted settlement under Ridgeline's Settlement Agreements defaults when a settlement payment is still unmade after its grace period, or when the number of returned payments on the settlement exceeds the programme's return limit.

**Clause 2 — The grace period.** A settlement defaults for an unmade payment only when the handling date is later than the grace period counted from that payment's due date. The grace period is the programme's grace in calendar days, the day after the due date being day one, with the due date already moved by any extension. The comparison is "later than": the last day of grace is still within grace.

**Clause 3 — Effect of default.** On default the discount is lost: the remaining settlement balance is released, payments already made stay applied to the account, the full remaining balance due is owed again, and the account returns from arranged to active.

**Clause 4 — The release.** A remainder is released only for a settlement whose status is defaulted or withdrawn, once, for the whole settlement balance remaining. The settlement balance is the settlement amount less settlement payments received, plus payments returned.

**Clause 5 — After default.** A default notice is sent, and a new offer on the account waits for the re-offer cooling-off period.

## Boundary cases for clause 2 (hypothetical, 5-day grace)

| Handling date, counted from the payment's due date | Payment still unmade | Defaults for that payment |
|---|---|---|
| The 5th calendar day after the due date | yes | no — still within grace |
| The 6th calendar day after the due date | yes | yes |
| The 6th calendar day after a due date that an extension moved | yes | yes, counted from the moved due date |

## Hypothetical worked example of the release

A hypothetical accepted settlement of 1200.00 dollars has received 400.00 dollars, of which none was returned, when it defaults. The settlement balance remaining, 800.00 dollars, is released in one entry; the 400.00 dollars paid stays applied to the account, and the account's full remaining balance due is owed again.

## Points of judgement

- **Does the consumer keep the settlement percentage after default?** No; the discount is lost.
- **Is the remainder released in parts?** No; once, for the whole settlement balance remaining.
